subject: Crypto control plane — operator escrow & rotation scenario review
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Alex Ruiz <alex.ruiz@acme.com>
Cc: Acme SecOps <security@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Jun 2028 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Crypto control plane — operator escrow & rotation scenario review

Team / Alex —

Attaching the first-pass architecture and runbook for the private-deploy crypto control plane we discussed. This thread is to capture decision points around: escrow model, operator separation, emergency unseal flows, and rotation cadence/automation. Please review attachments and the two decision options called out below; aiming to lock these choices before the customer cutover in July.

Attachments: crypto-controlplane-v1.pdf, operator-oncall-runbook.md, escrow-kek-matrix.xlsx
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-crypto-ctrlplane
Jira: JIRA-SEC-6421

High level (no changes to customer data plane):
- Customer controls tenant encryption keys (BYOK) using an HSM-backed KMS. Redwood runs the crypto control plane that performs unseal/wrap operations only under strictly defined flows.
- Two escrow options presented in the diagram:
  * Option A — Split-escrow (3-of-5) with offline escrow holders (customer security + two third-party escrow custodians). Keys are split and stored ciphertext-only; reconstruction requires physical or multi-channel operator steps.
  * Option B — Proxy-wrapped ephemeral unseal: Redwood holds a wrapping key in an HSM; customer-provided KEK (BYOK) wraps per-tenant KEKs. On emergency unseal we issue short-lived, attested unseal tokens to operator tooling; no long-term plaintext key storage on Redwood side.

Decision points we need feedback on from security/ops:
1) Which escrow model to standardize as the default for enterprise Private deploys? (A: split-escrow for maximum customer control vs B: proxy-ephemeral for faster recovery and simpler operator ergonomics)
2) Emergency unseal flow: do we require physical multi-admin ceremony + out-of-band approval for any >30-minute outage, or allow automated attestation-based unseal if multi-factor attestation succeeds?
3) Rotation cadence: recommend automated rolling every 90 days with immediate forced rotation after any operator-initiated unseal. Impact analysis and token/session invalidation steps are in the runbook.

Please call out any gaps in the runbook (operator oncall steps, audit events to emit, telemetry slices to keep). Alex / Acme — specifically: will Option A's offline escrow model increase your procurement/physical custody constraints?

Next steps: collect feedback by EOD Thu (6/20). I can schedule a short walkthrough on Fri if needed.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Product Security Manager
Redwood Inference

---

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Alex Ruiz <alex.ruiz@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Jun 2028 18:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Crypto control plane — operator escrow & rotation scenario review

Vanessa —

Quick skim and initial comments (I put inline notes in the runbook; high level below):
- Strong preference for Option B (proxy-wrapped ephemeral unseal) as our baseline for most customers. Reason: Option A operationally increases recovery friction and creates a higher risk of human error during reconstruction ceremonies.
- If we standardize on B we need two solid guarantees before we can sign off:
  1) The wrapping key in Redwood's HSM must be attested and rotated under a strict KMS policy; we should emit hardware attestation statements to the customer on each unseal event.
  2) Ephemeral unseal tokens must be single-use, short lived (<=5 minutes), and tied to an operator certificate bound to a specific signed runbook step.
- For catastrophic scenarios, we still should offer a documented split-escrow as an optional add-on (customer-requested). The runbook should include a tested rehearsal checklist for split-escrow (how to reconstruct, escrow holder contact matrix, and time-to-reconstruct SLIs).

I'll paste a couple of short inline edits I made to operator-oncall-runbook.md: add explicit audit event ids for: key-wrap-request, unseal-attestation, escrow-reconstruct-start, escrow-reconstruct-complete. Also added a note to invalidate all active sessions/token caches immediately after a forced rotation.

Happy to discuss on Fri.

—Marcus
Platform Security Lead
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Ruiz <alex.ruiz@acme.com>

Cc: Acme SecOps <security@acme.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 Jun 2028 09:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Crypto control plane — operator escrow & rotation scenario review

Vanessa / team —

Thanks for the detailed docs. A few clarifying Qs from Acme SecOps: 

1) If we go with Option A (split-escrow), can the escrow holders be provisioned across two physical regions (east/west) so the reconstruction ceremony tolerates a regional outage? We are comfortable with physical custody but want to avoid a single-region hot-site.

2) For Option B, please confirm the audit trail will include: unseal request timestamp, operator identity (cert thumbprint), HSM attestation blob, and the exact wrapped-key fingerprint returned to the customer. We will need these items for our internal auditors.

3) What are the SLAs for forced rotation and emergency key rewrap? Acme requirement is maximum 4 hours from approved unseal to fully rotated and re-encrypted tenant data. Is that achievable under Option B?

Also linking our procurement PO and the e-sign link for the addendum: https://app.docusign.com/agreements/abc123 — please confirm who from Redwood will sign.

If we can get the audit examples and a short checklist for regional escrow holders, we'll be able to confirm the model later this week.

Cheers,
Alex Ruiz
Head of SecOps
Acme Corporation

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Ruiz <alex.ruiz@acme.com>, Acme SecOps <security@acme.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Jun 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Crypto control plane — operator escrow & rotation scenario review

Alex —

Great questions. Summary / decisions based on thread and Marcus' inline edits: 

Decisions we are moving forward with (unless an objection is raised by EOD today):
- Default: Option B (proxy-wrapped ephemeral unseal) as the standard delivery for Private deployments.
- Optional: Option A (split-escrow across multi-region custodians) offered as a paid add-on; if chosen it will include a documented rehearsal and an SLA that reflects the higher recovery time.
- Emergency unseal: allow automated attestation-based unseal for outages <=30 minutes when an approved multi-factor attestation chain is observed; for >30 minutes require a two-person physical ceremony or out-of-band dual-approval.
- Rotation: automated rolling every 90 days; forced rotation after operator-initiated unseal. We will invalidate token caches and issue session revocations as Marcus suggested.

Action items:
1) Marcus / Platform Security — add attestation blob and HSM evidence snippets to the audit examples (due EOD Thu).
2) Soojin / Ops — draft the regional escrow-holder checklist and contact matrix for Option A (due Thu).
3) Monica / Compliance — produce an SLA snippet showing forced rotation within 4 hours under Option B with the required customer approvals (due Thu).
4) Vanessa — schedule walkthrough and include Acme procurement contact for DocuSign signature.

Provisional timeline: walkthrough Fri 6/21 9:00am PT; finalize runbook and push to the drive folder by Monday 6/24.

Forwarding Marcus' inline notes for visibility and tagging him for attestation/event ids.

Thanks everyone — please reply only if you have a blocking objection.

Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Product Security Manager
Redwood Inference
